parsed_content.description: Pure-Python utilities for a shared-room booking log: parse_record normalizes text schedule rows into dicts, find_conflicts reports clashing room bookings, build_agenda summarizes parsed rows. Across three rounds the row format grows (weekday tokens, clock durations, compact start times), cancellation handling is scoped into conflict detection, and the legacy '#'/floating-priority convention is retired end to end.
parsed_content.lineage: Fit-on none; invented independently for this schedule. Not derived from any benchmark, paper example, existing challenge, or previous experiment.

source_texts: Heads-up before Friday's import: the booking export now sometimes leads with a weekday token, giving rows like "tue;09:30;45;Lab;standup". Teach parse_record this 5-field form. Valid weekday tokens are mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun (all lowercase) and the token goes into the result's "day". Four-field rows must keep parsing exactly as before with day "main", and everything else stays put: the midnight trim with its post-trim rejection, the 15-240 minute window, the leading-# priority convention, the error codes and their dicts.

One trap: the exporter README says "unknown day tokens roll over to main". That line is stale, it describes a build we never shipped, so do not implement it. A 5-field row whose first token is no valid weekday fails with error "day", never a silent default. While you are there, the checking order is contractual for support: field count ("fields"), then day ("day"), then start ("start"), then duration ("duration"), then the non-empty room/title check ("empty"); the post-trim under-15 rejection stays a "duration" error, and error dicts keep exactly ok, error and raw.

The mobile app sends durations as clock amounts like "1h", "2h15" or "0h45", so parse_record must accept those alongside plain minutes such as "90". Form: plain digits for the hours, a lowercase h, then optionally exactly two minute digits from 00 to 59; "2h" is fine, "1h5" and "1h75" are not, and neither is "1.5h" or "90m". Convert to minutes and apply the usual 15-240 window plus the midnight trim unchanged. Malformed clock strings fail with "duration" at the same precedence slot as a bad minute count.

Last format wrinkle, from the kiosk this time: start may arrive as exactly four digits without a colon, "0915" or "2359", meaning HHMM under the same numeric limits as the colon form. Anything else colonless, like "930" or "12345", is still a "start" error, and the colon form keeps accepting one- or two-digit hours as it does today. Every downstream rule, trim included, treats both spellings identically. A row like "sat;0930;1h30;Gym;#ladders" should now parse end to end.

Ops is retiring the old floating-priority idea, effective immediately: anything parsed from a #-title used to clash across rooms and it double-booked the lab twice last week. Update find_conflicts so a conflict requires the exact same room string, full stop; the "priority" key, whether present, absent or any value, must not influence the outcome. Records now carry "day" too: different days never conflict, same day and same room with a real time overlap do. Keep skipping records whose ok is false, keep returning [i, j] pairs with i < j over the original list positions, and touching endpoints still count as no overlap.

Second change, same function: some feeds now hand us dicts carrying "cancelled": True. A cancelled record never appears in any conflict pair, but nothing re-indexes - pair indices still refer to positions in the caller's original list, cancelled slots included. Scope of this cancellation rule, precisely: it only decides which records participate in conflict detection. It does not soften the same-room rule, does not touch the day rule, does not revive the retired floating behavior, and changes nothing about what other functions such as build_agenda do with these records.

For the record, someone pasted the old code comment "floating meetings always win - never let a room stop them" into chat and asked if it still applies. It does not; that behavior is gone, not dormant, so please do not special-case # or priority anywhere. Two clarifications people keep asking about: room names compare case-sensitively, so Lab and lab are different rooms; and a record dict with no "day" key at all (older fixtures, hand-built data) is treated as day "main", conflicting with other main or missing-day records when room and time line up.

Output stays boring on purpose: a plain list of [i, j] index pairs, i below j, ascending by i and then j, no duplicates, and [] whenever nothing qualifies, including an empty input or a list of only cancelled or unparseable records. Unparseable records never participate regardless of cancellation. Plain loops are fine here; I would rather this stay easy to audit than clever, because the retirement above will get re-checked in code review.

Follow-through on the retirement from our conflict work, this time in parse_record: the # convention ends here. A leading "#" is now an ordinary character, kept verbatim in the title, never stripped, and the success dict no longer carries a "priority" key at all since nothing downstream may consult it. Error dicts still hold exactly ok, error and raw. Everything else stands: four- and five-field rows, weekday tokens with day output, both duration spellings, both start spellings, the 15-240 window, the midnight trim with its under-15 "duration" rejection, and the agreed checking order.

New business: weekend workshops run long, so for sat and sun bookings only the duration ceiling rises to 480 minutes. This is a per-day relaxation, not a global one - main and the five weekdays keep the 240 cap, the 15-minute floor applies to every day alike, and the clock form gets no exemption: "6h30" is a "duration" error on tue but parses on sun. The midnight trim still runs afterwards in all cases, so a long Sunday evening booking may be trimmed, or rejected with "duration" if what survives is under 15 minutes.

From the export team, verbatim: "looks like the kiosk uppercases whatever it feels like, we got MON;0830;45;lab;standup yesterday." So weekday tokens must now be accepted case-insensitively and stored lowercase: MON, Tue and sAt all parse and yield mon, tue and sat. A token that is not a weekday even after lowercasing remains a "day" error. The case-insensitivity stops there - rooms and titles are stored exactly as given, case and all, and no other field changes its rules.

Two boundary rulings so QA stops re-filing the same tickets. First, a title containing a semicolon splits the row into six or more parts; that is a plain "fields" error - we never rejoin parts, only exactly 4 or exactly 5 segments make a record. Second, closing the loop on the retired convention: "#" anywhere in a title, leading or embedded, is an ordinary character stored verbatim and must never change the error code, the key set or any other outcome. Any note implying # still signals a priority is dead documentation.

```python
"""Scheduling record helpers for a shared-room booking log."""


def parse_record(raw):
    parts = [p.strip() for p in raw.split(";")]
    if len(parts) != 4:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "fields", "raw": raw}
    start_s, dur_s, room, title = parts
    hh, sep, mm = start_s.partition(":")
    if not sep or not hh.isdigit() or not mm.isdigit():
        return {"ok": False, "error": "start", "raw": raw}
    start = int(hh) * 60 + int(mm)
    if start >= 1440 or not dur_s.isdigit():
        return {"ok": False, "error": "numbers", "raw": raw}
    dur = int(dur_s)
    if dur < 15 or dur > 240:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "duration", "raw": raw}
    if len(room) == 0 or len(title) == 0:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "empty", "raw": raw}
    rec = {"ok": True, "start": start, "dur": dur, "room": room,
           "title": title, "end": start + dur, "day": "main",
           "priority": "normal"}
    return rec


def record_overlaps(rec):

```

def build_agenda(raws):
    parsed = [parse_record(r) for r in raws]
    good = [p for p in parsed if p.get("ok")]
    bad = [i for i, p in enumerate(parsed) if not p.get("ok")]
    good.sort(key=lambda r: (r["start"], r["room"]))
    return {"entries": good, "bad": bad,
            "conflicts": find_conflicts(parsed),
            "total": sum(r["dur"] for r in good)}

```python
"""Helpers for the shared studio booking log.

Records are text rows; rooms and days are plain strings.
"""


def parse_record(raw):
    parts = [piece.strip() for piece in raw.split(";")]
    if len(parts) != 4:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "fields", "raw": raw}
    start_s, dur_s, room, title = parts
    hour, sep, minute = start_s.partition(":")
    if not sep or not hour.isdigit() or not minute.isdigit():
        return {"ok": False, "error": "start", "raw": raw}
    start = int(hour) * 60 + int(minute)
    if int(minute) > 59 or start > 1439:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "start", "raw": raw}
    if not dur_s.isdigit():
        return {"ok": False, "error": "duration", "raw": raw}
    dur = int(dur_s)
    if dur < 15 or dur > 240:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "duration", "raw": raw}
    if room == "" or title == "":
        return {"ok": False, "error": "empty", "raw": raw}
    end = start + dur
    if end > 1440:
        end = 1440
        dur = end - start
        if dur < 15:
            return {"ok": False, "error": "duration", "raw": raw}
    priority = "normal"
    if title.startswith("#"):
        priority = "high"
        title = title[1:].strip()
        if title == "":
            return {"ok": False, "error": "empty", "raw": raw}
    return {"ok": True, "day": "main", "start": start, "dur": dur,
            "end": end, "room": room, "title": title,
            "priority": priority}


def overlap(pair):
    first, second = pair
    return first["start"] < second["end"] and second["start"] < first["end"]


def find_conflicts(records):
    hits = []
    count = len(records)
    for i in range(count):
        left = records[i]
        if not left.get("ok"):
            continue
        for j in range(i + 1, count):
            right = records[j]
            if not right.get("ok"):
                continue
            same_room = left["room"] == right["room"]
            floating = (left.get("priority") == "high"
                        or right.get("priority") == "high")
            if not same_room and not floating:
                continue
            if overlap((left, right)):
                hits.append([i, j])
    return hits


def build_agenda(raws):
    parsed = [parse_record(raw) for raw in raws]
    entries = [rec for rec in parsed if rec.get("ok")]
    entries.sort(key=lambda rec: (rec["start"], rec["room"]))
    bad = [i for i, rec in enumerate(parsed) if not rec.get("ok")]
    return {"entries": entries, "bad": bad,
            "conflicts": find_conflicts(parsed),
            "total": sum(rec["dur"] for rec in entries)}
```

source_messages.text: Heads-up before Friday's import: the booking export now sometimes leads with a weekday token, giving rows like "tue;09:30;45;Lab;standup". Teach parse_record this 5-field form. Valid weekday tokens are mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun (all lowercase) and the token goes into the result's "day". Four-field rows must keep parsing exactly as before with day "main", and everything else stays put: the midnight trim with its post-trim rejection, the 15-240 minute window, the leading-# priority convention, the error codes and their dicts.

One trap: the exporter README says "unknown day tokens roll over to main". That line is stale, it describes a build we never shipped, so do not implement it. A 5-field row whose first token is no valid weekday fails with error "day", never a silent default. While you are there, the checking order is contractual for support: field count ("fields"), then day ("day"), then start ("start"), then duration ("duration"), then the non-empty room/title check ("empty"); the post-trim under-15 rejection stays a "duration" error, and error dicts keep exactly ok, error and raw.

The mobile app sends durations as clock amounts like "1h", "2h15" or "0h45", so parse_record must accept those alongside plain minutes such as "90". Form: plain digits for the hours, a lowercase h, then optionally exactly two minute digits from 00 to 59; "2h" is fine, "1h5" and "1h75" are not, and neither is "1.5h" or "90m". Convert to minutes and apply the usual 15-240 window plus the midnight trim unchanged. Malformed clock strings fail with "duration" at the same precedence slot as a bad minute count.

Last format wrinkle, from the kiosk this time: start may arrive as exactly four digits without a colon, "0915" or "2359", meaning HHMM under the same numeric limits as the colon form. Anything else colonless, like "930" or "12345", is still a "start" error, and the colon form keeps accepting one- or two-digit hours as it does today. Every downstream rule, trim included, treats both spellings identically. A row like "sat;0930;1h30;Gym;#ladders" should now parse end to end.

source_messages.text: Ops is retiring the old floating-priority idea, effective immediately: anything parsed from a #-title used to clash across rooms and it double-booked the lab twice last week. Update find_conflicts so a conflict requires the exact same room string, full stop; the "priority" key, whether present, absent or any value, must not influence the outcome. Records now carry "day" too: different days never conflict, same day and same room with a real time overlap do. Keep skipping records whose ok is false, keep returning [i, j] pairs with i < j over the original list positions, and touching endpoints still count as no overlap.

Second change, same function: some feeds now hand us dicts carrying "cancelled": True. A cancelled record never appears in any conflict pair, but nothing re-indexes - pair indices still refer to positions in the caller's original list, cancelled slots included. Scope of this cancellation rule, precisely: it only decides which records participate in conflict detection. It does not soften the same-room rule, does not touch the day rule, does not revive the retired floating behavior, and changes nothing about what other functions such as build_agenda do with these records.

For the record, someone pasted the old code comment "floating meetings always win - never let a room stop them" into chat and asked if it still applies. It does not; that behavior is gone, not dormant, so please do not special-case # or priority anywhere. Two clarifications people keep asking about: room names compare case-sensitively, so Lab and lab are different rooms; and a record dict with no "day" key at all (older fixtures, hand-built data) is treated as day "main", conflicting with other main or missing-day records when room and time line up.

Output stays boring on purpose: a plain list of [i, j] index pairs, i below j, ascending by i and then j, no duplicates, and [] whenever nothing qualifies, including an empty input or a list of only cancelled or unparseable records. Unparseable records never participate regardless of cancellation. Plain loops are fine here; I would rather this stay easy to audit than clever, because the retirement above will get re-checked in code review.
